close_reason: Closed in single doc pass commit. The new '# Contract guarantees' (or '# Features') section in pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs covers this finding.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs module rustdoc, from_cert / from_pem / from_der / from_der_iter / from_pem_file / from_der_file rustdoc — none of these surfaces explicitly state that the loader does NOT verify any signature on the trust-anchor certificate. Self-signed roots are the typical input, and a caller might reasonably (but incorrectly) assume that loading verifies the cert's own self-signature as a basic sanity check.

What actually happens: from_cert extracts subject + SPKI + name_constraints and discards the rest of the certificate including the signature. A trust-anchor file with arbitrary tampering — a swapped SPKI inside an otherwise-syntactically-valid TBS — loads cleanly and is then trusted by validate_path.

This is correct per RFC 5280 §6.1 (trust anchors are just (name, key, optional constraints) tuples; they need not be self-signed certs and the signature is not part of the path-validation algorithm). The crate's behavior is RFC-conformant. The concern is doc-level: a security reviewer or a downstream user reading only pkix-truststore (without first reading pkix-path) will not see this stated.

Defense-in-depth fix: add a paragraph to the module-level rustdoc and to from_pem / from_pem_file:

> # Trust-anchor file integrity
>
> These loaders extract (subject, SPKI, NameConstraints) from each certificate
> in the input and do NOT verify any signature on the certificate itself.
> A trust-anchor certificate's self-signature (or signature from an offline
> root) is not checked here. Trust in the loaded anchors derives entirely
> from trust in the input bytes: ensure the trust-anchor file is sourced from
> an authenticated channel (signed package, code-signed installer, IaC
> with file-hash pinning, etc.).

What goes wrong if undocumented: a deployer assumes "I'm loading from a CA bundle, the library will tell me if any cert is bad" and skips out-of-band integrity checks on the file. Attacker swaps the bundle, all bytes parse, validation proceeds against attacker's anchors. The loader behaved correctly per its contract; the contract was not communicated.

Adjacent to PKIX-tit4.1 but a different class: that one is fail-open on a parsed-but-malformed extension; this one is the broader observation that no integrity check on the file itself is part of the contract.

Engineering basis: principled crypto-API documentation states what is NOT done as well as what is done. rustls-pemfile, openssl::x509, and pyca/cryptography all make this explicit.
title: Rustdoc does not state that loaders do NOT verify trust-anchor self-signatures; file integrity is implicit caller responsibility
